<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />however, only one of these two conjugations is in use, or else they differ from one another in meaning, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד|translate=gravem esse}}, Piʿēl ''to honour'', Hiphʿîl ''to bring to honour'', also ''to make heavy''. Verbs which are intransitive in {{GHGterm|Qal}} simply become transitive in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָטָה|translate=to bow oneself}}, Hiph. ''to bow, to bend''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|d}}
Among the ideas expressed by the ''causative'' and ''transitive'' are included, moreover, according to the ''Hebrew'' point of view (and that of the Semitic languages in general, especially Arabic), a series of actions and ideas, which ''we'' have to express by periphrasis, in order to understand their being represented by the Hiphʿîl-form. To these ''inwardly transitive'' or ''intensive'' Hiphʿîls belong: (''a'') Hiphʿîl stems which express the obtaining or receiving of a concrete or abstract quality. (In the following examples the {{GHGterm|Qal}} stems are given, for the sake of brevity, with the addition of the meaning which—often together with other meanings—belongs to the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}.) Thus {{GHGheb|text=אהל}}, {{GHGheb|text=זהר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יפע}}, {{GHGheb|text=צוץ|translate=to be bright, to shine}} (to give forth brightness); opposed to {{GHGheb|text=חשׁךְ|translate=to become dark}}; {{GHGheb|text=אמץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=גבר}}, {{GHGheb|text=חזק|translate=to be strong}} (to develop strength), {{GHGheb|text=עטף|translate=to be weak}}; {{GHGheb|text=ארךְ|translate=to be long}} (to acquire length); {{GHGheb|text=גבהּ|translate=to be high}}; {{GHGheb|text=הום|translate=to be in tumult}}, {{GHGheb|text=זעק|translate=to cry out}}, {{GHGheb|text=רוע}}, {{GHGheb|text=רנן|translate=to make a noise, to exult}}; {{GHGheb|text=חלף|translate=to sprout}} (to put forth shoots), cf. {{GHGheb|text=פרח|translate=to bloom}}, {{GHGheb|text=עדף}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוק|translate=to overflow}}; {{GHGheb|text=חרשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=חשׁה}}, {{GHGheb|text=סכת}}, {{GHGheb|text=צמת|translate=to be silent}} (silentium facere, Pliny); {{GHGheb|text=מתק|translate=to be sweet}}; {{GHGheb|text=צלח|translate=to have success}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁפל|translate=to be low}}; {{GHGheb|text=אדם|translate=to become red}}, {{GHGheb|text=לבן|translate=to become white}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|e}}
(''b'') Stems which express in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the entering into a certain condition and, further, the being in the same: {{GHGheb|text=אמן|translate=to become firm, to trust in}}; {{GHGheb|text=באשׁ|translate=to become stinking}}; {{GHGheb|text=זוד|translate=to become boiling, to boil over}}; {{GHGheb|text=חלה|translate=to become ill}}; {{GHGheb|text=הסר|translate=to come to want}}; {{GHGheb|text=חרה|translate=to become hot}}; {{GHGheb|text=יבשׁ|translate=to become dry, to become ashamed}}; {{GHGheb|text=יתר|translate=to attain superiority}}; {{GHGheb|text=סכן|translate=to become familiar}}; {{GHGheb|text=עור}}, {{GHGheb|text=קוץ|translate=to become awake}}; {{GHGheb|text=קשׁה|translate=to become hard}}; {{GHGheb|text=רגע}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁקט|translate=to become quiet}} (to keep quiet); {{GHGheb|text=שׁמם|translate=to be astonished}}. The Hiphʿîl forms of some verbs of motion constitute a variety of this class: {{GHGheb|text=נגשׁ|translate=to draw near}}; {{GHGheb|text=קרב|translate=to come near}}; {{GHGheb|text=רחק|translate=to withdraw far off}} (all these three are besides used as causatives); {{GHGheb|text=קדם|translate=to come before}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|f}}
(''c'') Stems which express action in some particular direction: {{GHGheb|text=חטא|translate=to err}}; {{GHGheb|text=חלק|translate=to flatter}} (to act smoothly); {{GHGheb|text=יטב|translate=to act well, to do good}}; {{GHGheb|text=סכל|translate=to act foolishly}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׂכל|translate=to act wisely}}; {{GHGheb|text=ערם|translate=to act craftily}}; {{GHGheb|text=צנע|translate=to act submissively}}; {{GHGheb|text=רעע}}, {{GHGheb|text=רשׁע|translate=to act wickedly, godlessly}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁחת}}, {{GHGheb|text=תעב|translate=to act corruptly, abominably}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁלם|translate=to act peacefully, to be at peace, to be submissive}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|g}}
Further, there are in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} a considerable number of ''denominatives'' which express the ''bringing out'', the ''producing'' of a thing, and so are properly regarded as causatives,<ref>The same ideas are also paraphrased by the verb {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂה}} (''to make''), e.g. ''to make fat'', for, to produce fat upon his body, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=27}}; ''to make fruit, to make branches'', for, to put forth, to yield, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=7}}, cf. the Lat. ''corpus, robur, sobolem, divitias facere'', and the Ital. ''far corpo, far forze, far frutto''.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אצר|translate=to set over the treasury}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=13}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=וָאְַֽצַוֶּה}} is to be read, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2}}); {{GHGheb|text=בכר|translate=to bring forth a firstborn}}; {{GHGheb|text=גשׁם|translate=to cause to rain}}; {{GHGheb|text=זרע|translate=to produce seed}}; {{GHGheb|text=ימן}} ({{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵימִין}}) ''to go to the right'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂמְאִיל|translate=to go to the left}}; {{GHGheb|text=פרס|translate=to get}} or ''to have hoofs''; {{GHGheb|text=קרן|translate=to get}} or ''to have horns''; {{GHGheb|text=שׁכל|translate=to produce abortion}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁלג|translate=to become snow-white}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁמן|translate=to grow fat}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁרשׁ|translate=to put forth roots}}, &c.; so also according to the ordinary acceptation {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֶזְנִ֫יחוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=6}}, ''they have become stinking'', from {{GHGheb|text=אֶזְנָח|translate=stinking}} or ''stench'', with retention of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} prosthetic, {{GHGpar|19|m}} (but see below, p).<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
